what_it_does: This paper presents a high-speed receiver circuit for data links that operate at 106 gigabits per second—the kind of ultra-fast connections inside data centers that move training data to AI accelerators. The challenge is that at these speeds, the signal path suffers severe distortion (over 20 decibels of attenuation and phase shifting), which corrupts the data. The receiver uses two adaptive filtering stages to fix this: a 3-tap feed-forward equalizer at the analog front-end (before converting to digital) that tries to undo the channel damage, combined with a speculative 1-tap decision-feedback equalizer that guesses the next bit before all data has arrived. This combination avoids timing conflicts while using less power than traditional approaches, and successfully recovers signals from channels with 21.2 decibels of distortion.
